what_its_for: Colestipol is used to lower high cholesterol (LDL or 'bad' cholesterol) in your blood. Lowering your cholesterol helps reduce your risk of heart disease, heart attack, and stroke. It works by binding to bile acids in your gut so your body removes more cholesterol from your blood.
how_to_take: Colestipol comes as granules (powder) or tablets. For granules: Always mix the powder with at least 3 ounces (90 mL) of liquid such as water, juice, soup, or a carbonated beverage. Stir well and drink it all. You can also mix it with cereal, applesauce, or crushed pineapple. Never swallow dry powder — it can cause choking. For tablets: Swallow tablets whole with plenty of water. Do not crush, chew, or cut them. Take colestipol with meals or shortly after eating. Take all other medications at least 1 hour BEFORE or 4 hours AFTER taking colestipol, because it can interfere with how other drugs are absorbed.
dosing: Adults typically start at 2 grams (granules) or 2 grams (tablets) once or twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to 16 grams per day in divided doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store colestipol at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the granule powder tightly closed in its container. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medications at the same time as colestipol, because it can prevent other drugs from being properly absorbed into your body. Always take other medicines at least 1 hour before or 4 hours after colestipol. Avoid a high-fat diet, as this can work against the cholesterol-lowering effects of the medicine. Avoid skipping doses or stopping the medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; unusual bleeding or bruising; black or bloody stools; severe constipation that does not improve; muscle pain or weakness; signs of vitamin deficiency such as unusual fatigue, bleeding gums, or bone pain; difficulty swallowing or choking (especially with the powder form). Also call your doctor if your constipation is bothersome, as they may recommend a stool softener or dietary changes.
when_it_works: Colestipol may start to lower your cholesterol within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. Your doctor will check your cholesterol levels regularly (usually after 4 to 6 weeks) to see how well the medicine is working. To get the full benefit, you must keep taking it every day, even if you feel fine. This medicine works best when combined with a heart-healthy diet and regular exercise.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Colestipol is generally considered safe during pregnancy but may reduce the absorption of important vitamins. Your doctor may recommend vitamin supplements. Children: The safety and dosing in children should be determined by a pediatrician. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more prone to constipation with this medication. Make sure to drink plenty of fluids and eat a fiber-rich diet. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine.
